record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one analyze solutions of the KPZ equation at more than one space-time point, rather than only single-point distributions or partial marginal information?

evidence.quote: Another open problem is to analyze solutions of KPZ at more than one space-time point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation on the real line,
   ∂_t h(t,x) = ½ ∂_x^2 h(t,x) + ½ (∂_x h(t,x))^2 + ξ(t,x),  t > 0, x ∈ ℝ,
where ξ is space-time white noise and the nonlinearity is interpreted via the Hopf–Cole transformation Z(t,x) = exp(h(t,x)), with Z solving the multiplicative stochastic heat equation
   ∂_t Z = ½ ∂_x^2 Z + Z ξ.
Fix an initial condition (for instance the narrow wedge initial data h(0,·) = "log δ_0", flat data h(0,x) ≡ 0, or two-sided Brownian data). For any finite collection of space-time points (t_1, x_1), …, (t_n, x_n) with t_i > 0, derive a tractable description (e.g. an explicit formula, Fredholm determinant representation, or integrable structure) for the joint distribution of the random vector
   (h(t_1, x_1), h(t_2, x_2), …, h(t_n, x_n)),
going beyond known one-point distributions and partial marginal information. In particular, obtain such a description in the multi-time setting (with the t_i not all equal), and analyze its large-time asymptotics and correlation structure.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: multi-point (equal-time) and multi-time joint distribution formulas for the KPZ fixed point (the 1:2:3 scaling limit) are known for narrow-wedge and flat initial data (Johansson–Rahman, Liu, Matetski–Quastel–Remenik, Baik–Liu), and recent work (2025) extends these to general compactly supported initial data. For the KPZ equation itself at finite time, results on two-time and multi-time correlations (Corwin–Ghosal–Hammond and others) exist, but explicit tractable joint multi-point distribution formulas at finite time remain only partially available. The problem is therefore partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Multipoint distributions of the KPZ fixed point with compactly supported initial conditions
status_evidence.snippet: First formula for the space-time joint distributions of the KPZ fixed point with general initial conditions of compact support, obtained via a 1:2:3 KPZ scaling limit of multipoint distribution formulas for TASEP.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-point space-time joint distributions of the KPZ fixed point have been derived for general compactly supported initial data.

status_evidence.title: KPZ equation correlations in time
status_evidence.snippet: Corwin, Ghosal, Hammond analyze time correlations of the KPZ equation, giving bounds on two-time joint distributions.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-time correlation analysis for the KPZ equation has been carried out, providing partial information beyond one-point distributions.

status_evidence.title: The KPZ fixed point
status_evidence.snippet: Matetski, Quastel, Remenik construct the KPZ fixed point and give explicit multipoint distribution formulas as Fredholm determinants.
status_evidence.claim: Equal-time multi-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point are explicitly known via Fredholm determinants.
